candidates.name: Thm 5.1: closedness of the positive-density part (density splitting)
paper_items: I21 density cutoff f_r + tangential estimate r^{-3} O(r^2) o(r)
candidates.statement: J-Hermitian closed 4-manifold. P(alpha) = int alpha_x(l) dlambda(x,l) a positive measure on unit complex-line bivectors, Q in L^2 anti-invariant, P+Q closed, mu(B_r(x)) <= C r^2 and angular moment I_r = iint_{d<r} |l - tau m|^2 <= C r^4. Then theta(x) = lim r^{-2} mu(B_r(x)) exists everywhere and P_E = 1_{theta>0} P is closed.

lean_backed.detail: The Lean proves the role-equivalent fact: for the separating (mu, Q) it builds summable logarithmic activations c_n = 2^-n log(1 + f_n/delta_n) along chosen scales, and proves that the restriction of the unit-measure current to the exceptional set {sum c_n = infinity} is closed (concentration_restriction_closed) and that the concentration f_n -> 0 off that set. The decisive angular x transverse Cauchy-Schwarz balance IS in Lean (separating_current_angular_transverse_limit: int sqrt(angular * radial) sqrt(transverse) -> 0). NOT in Lean: the density limit theta, the set E = {theta > 0}, tangent measures (Lemma 5.3 is replaced by integrability of the radial 'defect' term), and the abstract hypothesis set: every Lean lemma also assumes hann (P annihilates closed invariant forms), so the weaker-hypothesis statement of Thm 5.1 is not formalized. For a Lean speedup test the usable unit is ConcentrationActivationData + concentration_restriction_closed, specialized to separating currents.

test1.verdict: close variant exists: the conclusion (the positive-density/Lelong part of a positive (1,1)-type current is closed) is classical for closed positive currents (Siu + Skoda/El Mir) and already proved for closed positive currents on almost Kahler 4-manifolds (TWZZ2022 App. B, Elkhadhra 2014), both in L. What is new is the hypothesis (P not closed; only P + Q closed with Q in L^2 anti-invariant, plus quantitative mass and angular bounds) and the real-variable proof (no J-analytic structure, no psh potentials): the angular x transverse balance r^{-3} O(r^2) o(r) = o(1). No neighbour found for that exact hypothesis/proof combination in searches 1-12 below.
test1.searches: WebSearch (standard/extended), 2026-10-12: (1) Siu decomposition Lelong numbers almost complex J-analytic; (2) Bellettini tangent cones positive (1,1) almost complex density; (3) restriction of normal current to positive-density set closed / rectifiable part; (4) Alessandrini-Bassanelli psh currents Siu; (5) TWZZ appendix Siu decomposition; (6) Dabbek-Elkhadhra-El Mir / Skoda-El Mir restriction; (7) semi-calibrated currents almost monotonicity (Bellettini, Riviere-Tian, Pumberger); (8) Harvey-Lawson almost complex potential theory / Pali; (9) Demailly regularization, zero Lelong numbers nef, Lamari/Buchdahl; (10) Bassanelli cut-off theorem; (11) Dinh-Sibony dd^c-closed currents Siu; (12) exact title 2606.29680. final.justification: Stays N2. The conclusion is a known theorem form (Siu/Skoda-El Mir; and for exactly this manifold class, TWZZ2022 App. B with Elkhadhra2014, both in L) and the candidate is its hypothesis weakening from 'P closed' to 'P + Q closed with Q in L^2 anti-invariant'. The proof assembles classical GMT (monotonicity, tangent measures, smoothed-density cutoffs, slicing) with the paper's own angular bound; the genuinely new piece is the quantitative balance r^{-3} * sqrt(I_r) * sqrt(N_r) = r^{-3} O(r^2) o(r), a Cauchy-Schwarz pairing of two moments the argument already controls. A strengthened known theorem with an original, short estimate is the definition of a close variant, not a jump. Not capped by the templated-IH rule (no induction). What would promote it to N3: (a) an expert confirming that no Siu/Skoda-type closedness theorem exists for positive currents that are closed only modulo an L^2 (or any Sobolev) correction in any setting (Taubes' SW=>Gr current limits, semicalibrated cycles, dd^c-closed currents are the places to look), AND (b) Test 4 showing the step is rarely proposed when the first pairing's failure is shown. Confidence 0.7, not higher, because snippet-level access left TWZZ App. B and 2606.29680 unread in full.

provenance_flag.explanation: 342 cites four 2025-2026 works besides its own companion: LinZhou2025 (2503.15939), WZZZ2025 (2412.18361), LiNing2026 (2607.18778) and Kinnunen2026 (lecture notes). Snippet-level summaries of the three arXiv items show no AI disclosure and none contains C1-C5 (operator note, Monge-Ampere PDE, Kahler-form spaces). The fifth, OpenAIHypersymplectic2026 (= family 341), is model-produced but is dated after 342 and depends on it, so it is reuse, not precedent. Searches pairing the problem with ChatGPT / GPT-5 / OpenAI / AI-assisted, and with the release, found no model-produced prior work; snippets still describe Donaldson's question as open apart from TWZZ (b^+ = 1 / h^- = b^+ - 1), Taubes (generic J, b^+ = 1) and Li-Zhang (rational surfaces). P-C1.equivalence: Hit = a proposal that (i) splits P by a set defined through 2-dimensional density / concentration of mu (E = {theta > 0} or an exceptional set of divergent concentration, as in the Lean ConcentrationActivationData), AND (ii) asserts closedness of the restricted part (equivalently of T - P_E) under the hypothesis that only P + Q is closed. Partial (recorded, not counted): a Siu-type split without the closedness claim, or closedness asserted only by appeal to analytic structure. A proof sketch need not contain the r^{-3} O(r^2) o(r) balance; a second judge score records whether it does.
P-C1.notes: Because L contains Elkhadhra2014 and TWZZ2022 App. B, a high hit rate in the directed arm is expected and would confirm N2; the informative measurement is the open arm and whether proposals include a workable proof idea (balance) rather than only the statement.
